headword: {交代|こうたい}{選手|せんしゅ}

definitions.explanation: A player who enters a game to replace another player on the field. Used across team sports including soccer, baseball, basketball, and others.

examples.japanese: {交代|こうたい}{選手|せんしゅ}がベンチで{待機|たいき}している。
examples.english: The substitute players are waiting on the bench.

examples.japanese: {後半|こうはん}から{交代|こうたい}{選手|せんしゅ}が{投入|とうにゅう}された。
examples.english: Substitute players were brought in from the second half.

examples.japanese: {監督|かんとく}は{残|のこ}り{10分|じゅっぷん}で{交代|こうたい}{選手|せんしゅ}を{3人|さんにん}{送|おく}り{出|だ}し、{攻撃|こうげき}を{強化|きょうか}した。
examples.english: The manager sent in three substitutes with ten minutes remaining to strengthen the attack.

notes:
A compound of {交代|こうたい} (substitution, replacement) and {選手|せんしゅ} (player, athlete). Most commonly used in soccer, where teams are allowed a limited number of substitutions per match.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {交代|こうたい}{選手|せんしゅ}を{出|だ}す: to send in a substitute
- {交代|こうたい}{選手|せんしゅ}を{投入|とうにゅう}する: to bring on a substitute
- {交代|こうたい}{選手|せんしゅ}として{出場|しゅつじょう}する: to appear as a substitute
- {交代|こうたい}{選手|せんしゅ}が{活躍|かつやく}する: the substitute plays well

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {控|ひか}え{選手|せんしゅ}: reserve player — a player on the roster but not starting; broader than {交代選手|こうたいせんしゅ}
- {補欠|ほけつ}: reserve, alternate — often implies not being good enough to start
- {代打|だいだ}: pinch hitter — specific to baseball
